Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a solitary, well-circumscribed rounded nodule in the right upper lobe apex without evidence of rib fractures or other traumatic injuries, which aligns with the radiographic appearance of a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM). This vascular lesion is a known mimic of lung nodules and fits the clinical scenario where trauma was minor but imaging revealed an incidental vascular anomaly.
